messages:
Elaine W.: FYI — acme-corp Private deployment started getting intermittent 403s to KMS after yesterday's egress-hardening rollout. Customer hits keys/decrypt errors in prod. Ticket 9983.
Jordan M.: Can you paste a repro? Which host/namespace? Any tcpdumps? timeframe?
Elaine W.: Repro steps from customer:
1) app pod calls our control plane which then calls KMS to unwrap keys
2) control plane sees HTTP/1.1 403 from KMS
3) happens about 1-3x/min under load
They shared this curl:
```
curl -v -H \"Authorization: Bearer <token>\" https://kms.redwood.internal/v1/decrypt -d '{"cipher":"..."}'
```
Support Bot: ticket 9983 created: https://zendesk/9983
Shiv P.: Two quick suspects: NAT ephemeral port exhaustion or firewall dropping TLS ClientHello (SNI). Default-deny egress can drop traffic if source port translation or TLS passthrough gets interfered with.
Mike L.: Can someone run this from a repro host and paste outputs?
```
ss -tan state established '( sport = :https )' | wc -l
sudo conntrack -L | tail -n 40
sudo tcpdump -ni eth0 host kms.redwood.internal and tcp port 443 -w /tmp/kms.pcap
```
Jordan M.: Also need iptables/nft rules + NAT gateway autoscale group size. If NAT has limited public IPs ephemeral range can blow.
Elaine W.: Pasted sanitized conntrack snippet from customer: 
```
tcp      6 4294967295 src=10.0.12.34 dst=54.23.11.99 sport=39182 dport=443 ... ESTABLISHED
tcp      6 30 src=10.0.12.35 dst=54.23.11.99 sport=39183 dport=443 ... TIME_WAIT
... (many TIME_WAIT / CLOSE_WAIT entries)
```
SRE Oncall: Pattern looks like NAT ephemeral exhaustion + conntrack build-up. Short-term mitigation: add an egress allow rule for kms.redwood.internal IP ranges to bypass proxy/NAT for controlplane egress, and scale NAT instances.
Shiv P.: Long-term: we should design a dedicated egress path for controlplane->KMS with stable source IPs (or use elastic IPs per AZ) and conntrack tuning on border routers. Also audit whether any TLS interception (proxy doing MITM) is breaking client certs — mTLS could be stripped and KMS returning 403.
Elaine W.: Customer also says they don't see audit entries for the failed decrypts in their control plane audit. audit-engine, any gaps in log ingestion?
audit-engine: I see ~54 missing audit events for org acme-corp between 2026-03-15T18:02:00Z and 2026-03-15T18:18:00Z. Likely dropped at log-forwarder when egress was failing. Filed LOG-337 to track delivery retry and backlog.
Mike L.: I repro'd locally: when iptables default-deny is active, curl -> 403. When I add: `iptables -A OUTPUT -d 54.23.11.0/24 -p tcp --dport 443 -j ACCEPT` calls succeed immediately. Captured pcap shows TLS SYNs being retransmitted then server sends RST.
Jordan M.: Next actions: 
- Temporary: create egress allow rule for acme to KMS IP ranges (security approval required)
- SRE: scale NAT + tune conntrack timeout for TIME_WAIT backlog
- Security: review default-deny baseline and add explicit safe egress exceptions for controlplane+audit-forwarder
- Verify audit log delivery after egress fix (audit-engine)
SRE Oncall: Opening infra incident INC-4521 and starting NAT scale now. ETA ~25m.
Elaine W.: @Security please review and sign off on the temporary allowlist and the long-term runbook edits. We need to avoid repeating this across other private deployments.
Jordan M.: I'll draft a short postmortem once root cause confirmed (likely NAT/conntrack + firewall default-deny + log-forwarder fallback missing).
Elaine W.: Thanks all — ping me when security has reviewed and when audit logs are flowing again. :thumbsup:
